title: Wormholes, Einstein-Rosen Bridges, and Spacetime Shortcuts
executive_summary: A wormhole (Einstein-Rosen bridge) is a speculative structure linking disparate points in spacetime, based on a special solution of the Einstein field equations in general relativity.
image_caption: Conceptual diagram of an Einstein-Rosen bridge connecting distant spacetime regions.

key_sections.title: Einstein-Rosen Bridges
key_sections.content: First theoretical formulations by Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen in 1935 showed that black hole solutions in general relativity can mathematically connect to separate regions of space.

key_sections.title: Traversable Wormholes and Exotic Matter
key_sections.content: To keep a wormhole open for human traversal, theoretical calculations show it requires negative-energy 'exotic matter' to counteract gravitational collapse.

key_sections.title: Time Dilation and Closed Timelike Curves
key_sections.content: If one mouth of a traversable wormhole is accelerated to near light speed, general relativity predicts it creates a closed timelike curve—a theoretical path into the past.
